summary.headline: Tata Consumer Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 18% to over INR5,400 crores, with EBITDA up 27% and margin expanding 100 bps to 14.6%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 18% in Q4 FY26 with India UVG of 16%, and EBITDA grew 27%, lifting margin 100 bps to 14.6%. Full-year revenue crossed INR20,000 crores (up 15%), but full-year EBITDA margin contracted to 13.9% after a soft first half on high tea and US coffee costs. India tea was price-cut as tea costs fell, with tea margins now back to the target range. Management guided to 50-75 bps full-year margin expansion in FY27, double-digit top-line growth, and a stepped-up A&P ratio of 7.5-8.5%.

financial_highlights.change: Contracted YoY; EBITDA +12% for full year

Adjusted EPS now published from this quarter

segments.name: India Beverages
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR1,600 crores, +4% (volume +4%, revenue -1%) on tea price cuts; FY26 +8%. Tea FY26 revenue +6%; tea margins back to target after pricing and lower costs.

segments.name: India Foods
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +21% with volume +15%, driven by salt; FY26 +18%. Salt market share up ~100 bps; Sampann Q4 +69% and FY26 +46%, with Sampann FY26 ARR about INR1,600 crores.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Q4 +21% reported, +11% constant currency, led by US coffee; FY26 +16% reported, +9% constant currency. Shipments via Dubai disrupted in March hit Capital Foods exports. Starbucks same-store sales +5%, 502 stores after 23 net adds.

segments.name: Non-branded (soluble/coffee)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +41-43% in constant currency; FY26 +23-25%. Profitability normalised after last year's elevated pricing-driven margins.

segments.name: Growth businesses
segments.commentary: Crossed INR4,000 crores in FY26, +24%, 31% of India business; Q4 +33%, contributing 33% of India business. Organic India INR135 crores ARR and Capital Foods INR213 crores ARR; RTD INR260 crores; Tata Copper Plus +33% in Q4.

segments.name: Channels
segments.commentary: Modern trade +20% (15% of India business); e-commerce plus quick commerce +62% (19% of India business). Food services ARR INR170 crores, vending ARR INR100 crores, pharmacy ARR INR30 crores.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 EBITDA margin expansion of 50-75 bps is 'a given' per management; quarterly phasing will be seasonal.
Top-line growth expected at double digits in FY27, with EBITDA growing ahead of revenue.
A&P expected to normalise to 7.5-8.5% of sales; Q4 was slightly soft, and FY27 quarters will vary with seasonality.
Growth businesses expected to keep compounding at about 30% in the near to medium term.
Tea cost broadly flat versus last year for FY27 so far; no change to tea guidance. Arabica at $2.99 per lb, so US coffee margins expected to recover within about two months.
Tea target of mid-single-digit volume growth plus price/mix for mid-to-high single-digit revenue growth; management wants a higher volume number than Q4's 4%.
capex_capacity: Board approved capacity expansion for tea extracts, which is running at full capacity; project to start now.
Vietnam (soluble coffee) capacity running at about 99% utilisation; expansion to be online very early in 2027.
Go-to-market rollout fully complete: 64 core cities for salt and tea, and about 17 cities with common distributors; lines per outlet rising.
Distribution at about 2 million direct outlets with numeric reach of 4.5 million, versus 0.5 million and 2 million six years ago.
Starbucks: 502 stores in 80 cities after 23 net openings in the year.
demand_pricing: India beverage volume +4% but revenue -1% in Q4 because of tea price cuts passed on as costs fell.
Salt volume growth was strong, supported by a broad portfolio (zinc, iron, light, rock, sendha, solar, vacuum evaporated) and Tata Salt top-of-mind awareness of about 88.
Management said Nielsen does not capture quick commerce and e-commerce (about 21% of portfolio). Market share reporting will be stopped; salt share will still be tracked internally.
US coffee: Arabica pricing falling; industry margins expected to return to levels of about two years ago. Some promotional pricing risk on shop floors.
Campa (water competitor) aggressive pricing noted; management does not see a major price fight in affordable cups, and targets 30% growth for NourishCo.
Middle East disruption: shifted plastic closures and PET imports about 15-20 days earlier; LPG sourced from alternate suppliers or dual-use burners; no continuity issue reported.

qa_highlights.question: Will gross margins come under pressure from crude and fuel cost increases, and what margin should be expected for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said packaging and LPG costs have risen, but margins have not been hit materially so far. It is confident of EBITDA growing ahead of revenue and 50-75 bps full-year expansion, with pricing as a mitigation lever.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Sampann grow nearly 70%, and can its margin match the beverage and salt margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was broad-based across pulses, poha and vermicelli, helped by NPDs and quick-commerce/e-commerce reach. Sampann is heading to a mid-teens margin after promotion and advertising; salt is strong and beverages have recovered.

qa_highlights.question: Will the market share data be replaced, and how is performance benchmarked on e-commerce and quick commerce?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will stop publishing market share because the data misses e-commerce, quick commerce and half of modern trade. Benchmarking will use numeric reach and lines per outlet, and it still cites tea leadership in quick commerce.

qa_highlights.question: Is US coffee pricing at risk as commodity costs fall, and what is the long-term growth outlook for NourishCo?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins are expected to recover toward pre-upcycle levels over 2-3 months as inventory turns, though not necessarily fully. Management expects NourishCo to keep growing about 30%, across water, affordable cups and tea/coffee.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 4% tea volume growth satisfactory, and why is quick commerce so strong for Tata Consumer?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wants a higher tea volume number than 4% and aspires to beat mid-single-digit volume. Quick commerce is treated as the consumer-first channel where it can test and scale before rolling out to modern trade and general trade.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tea cost outlook for FY27 and will tea margins expand?
qa_highlights.answer: Tea costs are roughly flat year-on-year; the season started with auctions up in April. Q4 tea margins are roughly where management wants them, and it will react with pricing to commodity moves.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Capital Foods lag while Organic India grew about 26-27%?
qa_highlights.answer: Capital Foods was hit by the nationwide go-to-market relaunch in top cities between November and February, plus March shipping disruption via the Middle East. Organic India benefited from onshore US inventory built up earlier.

risks_watch: Middle East shipping disruption and LPG/fuel cost inflation could lead to broad-based inflation and pricing actions across the industry.
Non-branded and US coffee margins are still normalising; promotional pricing risk in the US is flagged.
Share data is no longer published, so external tracking of tea share becomes harder.
Capital Foods growth was below expectations in Q4; the 30% growth target depends on GTM execution.
Competition in water (Campa, NourishCo) and A&P normalisation to 7.5-8.5% could pressure margins.
A&P and margin trajectory: quarterly phasing is seasonal, so margin expansion may come unevenly through FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line and margin delivery, with explicit targets for FY27. Cautious on fuel and packaging inflation and reluctant to forecast commodities beyond the near term, but says pricing can offset costs.

But right now, we remain confident of delivering top line numbers and EBITDA ahead of top line, right?
No/ So 50 to 75, 80 bps is a given. I mean it's not an option. We will deliver it, number one.

growth.why: Management guides double-digit FY27 top-line growth with EBITDA ahead of revenue and 50-75 bps margin expansion, backed by Vietnam solubles capacity (99% utilised, online early 2027), an approved tea extract expansion, salt/Sampann momentum and growth businesses compounding ~30%, though no quantified capacity or order numbers were given for the top-line guide.
